<!-- ============ APPOINTMENT ============ -->
<section class="appointment" aria-labelledby="new-role">
  <div class="wrap appointment-grid">
    <div class="appointment-year">2026</div>
    <div>
      <h2 id="new-role">A new chapter at the Bureau</h2>
      <p>
        I have joined the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics as Member (Economic Statistics).
        For years my work has circled the same questions: how prices are measured,
        how industrial output is counted, and how official numbers can earn public trust.
        Now I get to work on them from the inside, alongside the people who produce Pakistan's
        official statistics.
      </p>
      <p>
        My portfolio covers economic statistics and, more recently, social statistics as well.
        My priorities are data literacy, both within the Bureau and among the people who use its
        numbers, and bringing machine learning and new data sources responsibly into the
        production of official statistics.
        <a href="posts/joining-pbs/index.html">Read the announcement</a>.
      </p>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- ============ FOCUS ============ -->
<section class="section" aria-labelledby="focus">
  <div class="wrap">
    <h2 id="focus" class="section-title">What I work on</h2>
    <p class="section-intro">Six threads run through my research, teaching and public writing.</p>
    <div class="focus-grid">
      <div class="focus">
        <h3>Measuring the economy</h3>
        <p>Price indices, GDP base-year revisions and industrial statistics. My 2008 paper on biases in Pakistan's CPI was one of the first systematic critiques of how we measure prices.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="focus">
        <h3>Official statistics for the data age</h3>
        <p>Machine learning in official statistics, multi-source and administrative data, and a national data infrastructure that connects surveys, registers and new digital sources.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="focus">
        <h3>Applied econometrics</h3>
        <p>Causal inference, graph-theoretic causality, time series and forecasting, published in Taylor &amp; Francis, Springer, SAGE and Elsevier journals.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="focus">
        <h3>AI and data governance</h3>
        <p>How public institutions can use AI responsibly, and why Pakistan's AI ambitions depend first on good data rather than hype.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="focus">
        <h3>Data skills for development</h3>
        <p>R, Quarto and reproducible research for economists, civil servants and students, with more than 60 open repositories of teaching material.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="focus">
        <h3>Human development</h3>
        <p>Food security, nutrition, health and education spending, studied through Pakistan's household surveys.</p>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>
